title: Incomplete key zeroization
provenance: Locally authored key register with an injected defect (zeroize erases only the low byte), modelled on CWE-1239. Written for SiliconBreak X; not a historical bug in any product.
license: Same license as this repository (authored here)
description: A 16-bit key register that feeds a crypto engine. Zeroize must erase every key bit; zeroize wins over a simultaneous load.

interface.text: capture key_in and mark the key valid
key presented to the crypto engine

security_contract.summary: Zeroization must remove all key material; no key bits may remain once the key is invalid.

properties.text: One cycle after zeroize, key_out == 0 and key_valid == 0 (zeroize wins over a simultaneous load).
Whenever key_valid == 0, key_out == 0: no part of a previous key remains visible.

functional_contract.text: Reset clears the key and key_valid.
load captures key_in into key_out and sets key_valid; the key is held until zeroize or reset.
After zeroize a new key can be loaded.

tests.title: Load captures and holds the key
3000 random cycles: valid keys match the contract model
Zeroize wins over a simultaneous load
No key bits reappear after zeroize

ground_truth.summary: The zeroize branch clears only key_q[7:0]; the upper key byte survives.
